subject: Post-call recap — unit-cost runway & ops levers
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@bluestonepay.com>, Priya Shah <priya@bluestonepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — unit-cost runway & ops levers

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same priorities. High-level takeaways from our call: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable token spend during peak reconciliation jobs plus a hard monthly budget cap for inference (~$35k/month).
- Goals: get to a predictable unit cost (cost per transaction) and validate a pilot that keeps latency within ~200ms P95 for customer-facing flows.
- Current footprint you shared: ~18–24M tokens/month today with daily spikes during settlement windows (up to 3x baseline).

What we discussed as levers and potential impact:
- Batching: expected 25–40% token-cost reduction for reconciliation/settlement backfills if we accept slightly higher internal latency windows.
- KV/prefix caching for repetitive prompts: 10–15% token reduction on common queries for the customer support flows.
- Model variant + 4-bit quantization for background jobs: 40–60% GPU cost reduction with small quality tradeoffs (we suggested a short eval).
- Smart routing: hot-path requests keep high-SLA models; background jobs route to cheaper variants.

Ask / next steps (proposed):
1) You (Alex/Priya) share a 48–72h anonymized traffic sample (we attached a sample format as expected-traffic-sample.json).
2) We will run a light cost model + sensitivity analysis (attached cost-model-v1.csv) and return a 1-page ROI snapshot.
3) Ops deep-dive (30–45m) next week to align on acceptable latency windows, rollout constraints, and SOC/compliance gating.

Proposed tentative date: Thu Oct 15, 10:00–10:45 PT — calendar link in the follow-up if that works.

Attachments: cost-model-v1.csv (stub), expected-traffic-sample.json (format).

Thanks — will keep the ask simple so procurement can evaluate quickly.

—
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@bluestonepay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@bluestonepay.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — unit-cost runway & ops levers

Appreciate the crisp summary, Grace — that's exactly what we need to evaluate next week. Quick confirmations: 

- Budget: the $35k/month cap is firm for Q4; if we show a path to 30–40% cost compression for background jobs we can get an exception for a 90-day pilot.
- SLA: customer-facing latency must remain <= 250ms P95 — so any routing/batching changes must preserve that.

I'll share the anonymized traffic sample by EOD Wednesday (we have to scrub some PII). Also putting procurement on standby for the ROI snapshot — they asked for an executive one-pager (simple before/after cost and recommended commit).

Two small asks from our side: 
1) Can you include a scenario in your cost model that shows the impact of 50% spike events (i.e., settlement day 2x–3x traffic) on expected monthly burn?
2) Any quick notes on security/retention differences between a hosted pilot vs. a dedicated pool — procurement will want to see options.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Nguyen
Product Lead, Core Payments | Bluestone Pay
alex.nguyen@bluestonepay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — unit-cost runway & ops levers

Grace — quick internal ops checklist before the deep-dive. I'm happy to run the technical portion of the call. Notes: 

- Request sample shape: we need token counts per request, sequence length distribution, timestamp (UTC), and a categorical flag for "background" vs "customer-facing". The attached format is good.
- For batching sensitivity: please confirm acceptable internal queuing window for reconciliation jobs (we should propose 500ms, 1s, and 5s buckets for modeling).
- Caching: we'll check how many prompt prefixes are high-frequency (top 200 keys) and simulate a KV cache hit-rate curve (10%, 25%, 50%).
- Quantization plan: we'll generate an eval harness comparing full-fp model vs 4-bit variant on a 200-example prompt set — need Bluestone to flag any prompts that are high-risk for hallucination/accuracy.

I'll prepare a short Ops slide deck (2–3 slides) showing the scenarios (baseline, moderate batching, aggressive batching+quantized background) with projected monthly spend and P95 impact.

If Alex/Priya share the sample, I'll run the sensitivity over the next 48 hours and drop a short ROI one-pager for procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@bluestonepay.com>, Priya Shah <priya@bluestonepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — unit-cost runway & ops levers

Thanks Alex — that timeline works. Two quick replies: 

- We'll include a 50% spike scenario in the cost sensitivity runs and show both absolute $ impact and percent deviation from baseline.
- Security/retention: short note for procurement — hosted pilot (Redwood API) keeps data encrypted at rest with KMS controls, default 30-day request logs retention; Dedicated pool option supports customer-managed keys and configurable retention (can be set to 90/30/0 days), which can be called out in the ROI doc as a procurement/ops delta. Marissa, please expand that on the Ops slide.

I've booked Thu Oct 15, 10:00–10:45 PT for the ops deep-dive and sent a calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/ops-deep-dive-8712

Next items from our side:
- Marissa to run sensitivity analysis once sample arrives and drop a 1-page ROI + 1-slide ops delta for procurement (delivery target: Fri Oct 16 EOD).
- Bluestone to deliver anonymized traffic sample (Wed Oct 14 EOD) and flag any high-risk prompts for the eval.

If anything changes on your side please ping — otherwise we'll see you on the 15th.

Thanks again,

—
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
